residencyRequirements.description: One of the parties must have been domiciled in Virginia, or been a bona fide resident of Virginia, for at least six months immediately preceding the filing of the suit.

withAgreementNoChildren.description: 6-month separation required if there are no minor children AND the parties have a signed separation agreement.

otherwise.description: 1-year separation required if the parties have minor children OR do not have a signed separation agreement.

noFault.name: Six-Month Separation (No Children + Separation Agreement)
noFault.description: The parties have lived separate and apart without any cohabitation for six months, there are no minor children of the marriage, and the parties have a signed property settlement or separation agreement.

noFault.name: One-Year Separation
noFault.description: The parties have lived separate and apart without any cohabitation and without interruption for one year.

fault.name: Adultery, Sodomy, or Buggery
fault.description: Respondent has committed adultery, sodomy, or buggery outside the marriage.
fault.notes: Adultery as grounds may affect spousal support eligibility

fault.name: Conviction of Felony
fault.description: Respondent has been convicted of a felony, sentenced to confinement for more than one year, and confined pursuant to such sentence.

fault.name: Cruelty, Desertion, or Abandonment
fault.description: Respondent has been guilty of cruelty, caused reasonable apprehension of bodily hurt, or willfully deserted or abandoned Petitioner.
fault.notes: Requires one-year waiting period after the act of cruelty or desertion

propertyDivision.description: Virginia is an equitable distribution state. Property is classified as separate, marital, or hybrid. The court equitably divides marital property considering 11 statutory factors. Separate property is generally not subject to division.

propertyClassification.maritalProperty: Property acquired during the marriage, other than by gift or inheritance from a third party
propertyClassification.separateProperty: Property acquired before marriage, or during marriage by inheritance or gift from a third party
propertyClassification.hybridProperty: Property that is part marital and part separate (transmutation principles apply)

factors: Contributions, monetary and nonmonetary, of each party to the well-being of the family
Contributions, monetary and nonmonetary, of each party to the acquisition and care and maintenance of marital property
Duration of the marriage
Ages and physical and mental condition of the parties
Circumstances and factors which contributed to the dissolution of the marriage
How and when specific items of marital property were acquired
Debts and liabilities of each spouse
Liquid or nonliquid character of all marital property
Tax consequences to each party
Use or expenditure of marital property by either of the parties for a nonmarital separate purpose or the dissipation of such funds
Such other factors as the court deems necessary or appropriate

spousalSupport.description: The court may award spousal support and maintenance to either party. Adultery by the receiving party may bar alimony. The award may be permanent, limited, or rehabilitative.
factors: Obligations, needs and financial resources of the parties
Standard of living established during the marriage
Duration of the marriage
Age and physical and mental condition of the parties
Extent to which the age, physical or mental condition, or special circumstances of any child would affect a party's ability to work
Contributions, monetary and nonmonetary, of each party to the well-being of the family
Property interests of the parties
Provisions made with regard to the marital property under § 20-107.3
Earning capacity of each party
Education and training of the parties and the time and costs to acquire sufficient education or training to enable the party seeking support to find appropriate employment
Decisions regarding employment, career, economics, education and parenting arrangements made by the parties during the marriage
Contributions, monetary and nonmonetary, of each party to the care and wellbeing of minor children during the marriage and any changes in circumstances subsequent to the entry of a final decree
Such other factors as are necessary to consider the equities between the parties

custody.description: Virginia courts apply a best-interests-of-the-child standard with 10 statutory factors. Courts may award joint or sole legal and physical custody.

childSupport.description: Child support is calculated under Virginia's income shares guidelines.

affidavitOfComplainant.name: Affidavit of Complainant (for no-fault divorce)
affidavitOfComplainant.notes: Required when proceeding without ore tenus hearing

financialStatement.name: Financial Statement
financialStatement.notes: Required when spousal support or child support is at issue

separationAgreement.name: Property Settlement Agreement
separationAgreement.notes: Strongly recommended to resolve property, support, and custody

filingFees.notes: Virginia circuit court filing fee for a divorce complaint is $86 per Va. Code § 17.1-275. Additional fees for service of process ($12-$25 for sheriff service). Fee waivers are available for qualifying individuals.

legalCitations.description: Grounds for divorce from the bond of matrimony — no-fault and fault-based grounds
Residency requirement — domicile in Virginia for 6 months
Equitable distribution of marital property — separate and marital property
Child custody — legal and physical custody

formattingRequirements.notes: Divorce is filed in Virginia Circuit Court. Virginia uses 'Bill of Complaint' for the initiating pleading and 'Final Decree of Divorce' for the judgment.

basic.name: Bill of Complaint for Divorce
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding in Virginia Circuit Court

basic.name: VS-4 Report of Divorce
basic.description: Vital statistics report required by the Virginia Department of Health

basic.name: Final Decree of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

service.name: Summons
service.description: Formal service on respondent (personal service or service by publication)

service.name: Acceptance/Waiver of Service
service.notes: Must be in writing and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Child Support Guidelines Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per Virginia Child Support Guidelines (Va. Code § 20-108.2)

withChildren.name: Parenting Plan / Custody and Visitation Agreement
withChildren.notes: Required when custody or visitation is contested

inState.description: Respondent must file a responsive pleading within 21 days of service

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside Virginia must file a responsive pleading within 21 days of service; additional time may be granted

childSupportGuidelines.description: Virginia uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross incomes are combined and matched to a statutory schedule. The basic support obligation is then divided between the parents in proportion to their incomes. Adjustments are made for health insurance, childcare, and extraordinary medical/dental expenses.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The guidelines are presumptive. The court may deviate upon a written finding that application of the guidelines would be unjust or inappropriate.

options: County or city where the parties last cohabited
County or city where the respondent resides
County or city where the complainant resides if the respondent is a non-resident or cannot be found
